concurrency/effect/Semaphore#never more.note: The original does it on 4.0.7 and 3.22.4: makeSemaphore(2) then release(1) leaves 3 free (taken -1). release(n) is `taken -= n` with no floor (Semaphore.ts:292-293; circular.ts:104), and releaseAll's own gotcha says the free count can exceed the configured permits (Semaphore.ts:165-170). The semaphore trusts its callers to release what they took: the law is stated too strongly, kept as a false law the prover must not prove. (The search's run reaches it through a negative resize and takeIfAvailable; release(1) on a fresh semaphore is the short one.)

concurrency/effect/Semaphore#what is tak.note: The original does it on both versions: two permits taken, resize(1) leaves free -1. resize sets the permits and does nothing more when free goes below 0 (Semaphore.ts:313-320, `if (this.free < 0) return internal.void`; circular.ts:93-102): a permit held stays held, by design. The law is stated wrong.

concurrency/effect/Semaphore#takeIfAvail.note: The original does it: on 4.0.7, makeSemaphore(2) then takeIfAvailable(-3) succeeds (true) and leaves 5 free; take(-3) does the same on 4.0.7 and 3.22.4 (`this.free < n` is false for a negative n, then `taken += n`, Semaphore.ts:237-239 and :284-290; circular.ts:46-68), and so would withPermits(-3) and withPermitsIfAvailable(-3). No count is checked to be at least 0, so a negative take is a release. Minor: an argument no caller should pass; whether it is the caller's error is upstream's call. Not reported (the user decides on disclosure).

ratelimit/effect/fixedWindow#a window ne.note: The original does it on 4.0.7: fixedWindow({tokens: 1, limit: 0}) twice replies [1, 1000] then [2, 2000], counting and extending the window past the limit given. The check is `options.limit && counter.count + options.tokens > options.limit` (RateLimiter.ts:750), so a limit of 0 reads as no limit, against the store's contract (:638-639, "If `limit` is provided, the number of taken tokens will be capped at the limit"). Minor: RateLimiter.consume never reaches it (with onExceeded "fail" a request of more tokens than the limit fails before the store, :112; with "delay" the limit is passed as undefined, :131), so only a direct caller of the store, or another store's author reading the memory store as the reference, meets it. Not reported (the user decides on disclosure).
